provenance.reference: synthetic-moon-motion/other-planets.py: DOP853 Sun + external catalogue perturbers; unchanged reference states; current build rows shift by -2 from original because preceding population count changed

objectsHeader.notes: Synthetic small bodies: statistical stand-ins for conditioned model deficits in (a, e, i, H) cells (the COMPLETE reality level). No orbit-specific survey detectability or observation veto is evaluated. Known attributes are synthetic; missing rotation is unknown.

a.label: synthetic
a.method: semimajor axis (about the Sun; about the planet-system barycentre for populations with a center)

H.label: synthetic
H.method: V-band absolute magnitude; G = 0.15 (Bowell et al. 1989 conventional value)

pV.label: synthetic
pV.method: quantile draw from measured but not selection-corrected albedo templates of real objects of the same population near the same a (attributePools); irregular moons: of real irregular moons of the planet (Grav et al. 2015)

rotPeriod.label: synthetic
rotPeriod.method: quantile draw from measured but not selection-corrected LCDB periods (U >= 2-) of real objects of similar diameter D = 1329 km / sqrt(pV) 10^(-H/5); NaN (unknown) for irregular moons

k.method: candidate number in the cell's stream (0-based; valid candidates only for model realizations, raw stream index for catalogue-extrapolated populations)

colorClass.label: synthetic
colorClass.method: index into smallbodies/core.json colorClasses: the class of the albedo template; 255 = no class, grey (header grey)

limit.rule: first H bin with known < model - 2 sqrt(model) (any e, i)
limit.uncertainty: Completeness limit is a proxy fitted from a/H bins (histogram peaks or model deficits), not a detection probability. Moon model deficits are fitted over H for the whole class and copied to each a bin; Uranus/Neptune have no faint model and no deficit cutoff. No pointing history, detection efficiency or per-object observation veto is used; survey detectability was not evaluated for this synthetic orbit. The Poisson deficit threshold does not include population-model normalization or systematic uncertainty.

model.motion: fixed two-body Kepler elements about the Sun (gmSun), not propagated through the app's catalogue force model; planetary perturbations are omitted.
model.positionUncertainty: Individual true position and omitted-force position budget for this object/viewpoint are unknown. Audit C3 table (docs/reports/synthetic-limitations.md): one representative trajectory's largest sampled fixed-Kepler drift against independent integration over 2025-04-04 to 2028-04-04: 167,263.0 km; Earth direction 81.6184 arcsec; Sun-centre direction 0.017459 deg; not a bound for this object, the population or arbitrary observers. Heliocentric comparison uses Sun and product perturbers' Newtonian forces (omits 1PN/J2/nongrav); moon comparison uses host gravity and differential solar gravity (omits J2/other moons). These historical samples do not certify another catalogue, epoch or window.
model.uncertainty: Conditional population approximation, not an exact unseen count. Albedo/colour and LCDB rotation templates are measured but not selection-corrected; no explicit H-dependent family model. Individual existence, shape and true orbit are unknown.

model.crossCheck: 'The population of Centaurs is estimated to be 21,000 +- 8,000 for D > 10 km' (abstract; H_r < 13.7 for a 6% albedo, a < 30 au, q > 7.5 au).
model.angles: 'As the output angular elements are uncorrelated with each other, and in order to avoid clustering of the orbits, the angular elements omega, Omega, and M are randomized U[0, 360)' (Sec. 2.3.1). The stage does the same: (a, e, i) from the reweighted model, angles uniform.

H_V.label: estimated
H_V.method: Recomputed Chandler §7 Eq.9–10 from the authors' coma-separated Johnson V=22.4 (their own nuclear g/r-to-V conversion via Jester et al. 2005), R=10.10 au, delta=10.01 au, alpha=5.58 deg, assumed G=0.15, A1=3.33, A2=1.87, B1=0.63, B2=1.22. H_V = V - 5 log10(R delta) + 2.5 log10[(1-G)Phi1 + G Phi2], Phi_i=exp[-Ai tan(alpha/2)^Bi]. The paper's reported H_V=11.3 is retained separately; it does not reproduce these inputs.
H_V.uncertainty: Approximate PSF decomposition, rounded published photometry/geometry and assumed G; systematic uncertainty not quantified. Computation precision is not measurement precision.

model.notModelled: Centaurs with a < 5.35 au (inside the Trojan grid) and a >= 30 au (the Kuiper-belt grid); the model has no members below a = 5.37 au.
model.motion: fixed two-body Kepler elements about the Sun (gmSun), not propagated through the app's catalogue force model; planetary perturbations are omitted.
model.positionUncertainty: Individual true position and omitted-force position budget for this object/viewpoint are unknown. Audit C3 table (docs/reports/synthetic-limitations.md): one representative trajectory's largest sampled fixed-Kepler drift against independent integration over 2025-04-04 to 2028-04-04: 215,404.0 km; Earth direction 12.3348 arcsec; Sun-centre direction 0.003297 deg; not a bound for this object, the population or arbitrary observers. Heliocentric comparison uses Sun and product perturbers' Newtonian forces (omits 1PN/J2/nongrav); moon comparison uses host gravity and differential solar gravity (omits J2/other moons). These historical samples do not certify another catalogue, epoch or window.
model.uncertainty: Conditional population approximation, not an exact unseen count. Albedo/colour and LCDB rotation templates are measured but not selection-corrected; no explicit H-dependent family model. Individual existence, shape and true orbit are unknown. Kurlander et al. 2025 §5.3 rejects their joint distribution. 43 catalogued comet-flagged Centaurs are not conditioned on: named qualifications, bounds and unknowns are in cometNuclei.objects. Catalogue M2 laws alone are not qualified bare-nucleus H. 18 catalogue M2 laws are retained; their bare-nucleus suitability remains unestablished. 1 qualified nuclei counted. 1.0% of model states are not recovered by the archive weighting. Kurlander et al. 2025 normalization: 21400 (+3400/-2800) with H_r < 13.7; conditional on that joint model.
model.method: Literature orbit model of Nesvorny et al. 2019 with independent Lawler et al. 2018 H law, normalized by Kurlander et al. 2025; magnitude-selected archive reweighted by 1/P(selected | distance modulus), under that law. This is not the survey's orbit-sensitive efficiency. Only sourced, qualified point nuclear H_V counts inside represented a/e/i/H cells and a/H groups. M1, unqualified M2, coma lower bounds and unknown object-specific band conversions do not count.

populations.name: irregular-jupiter

limit.rule: first H bin (bright to faint, inside the model's range) where the known moons of the class number fewer than model - 2 sqrt(model)

calibration.rule: H_V = m + offset (median of H_MPC - m over the calibrators)

limit.uncertainty: Completeness limit is a proxy fitted from a/H bins (histogram peaks or model deficits), not a detection probability. Moon model deficits are fitted over H for the whole class and copied to each a bin; Uranus/Neptune have no faint model and no deficit cutoff. No pointing history, detection efficiency or per-object observation veto is used; survey detectability was not evaluated for this synthetic orbit. The Poisson deficit threshold does not include population-model normalization or systematic uncertainty.

model.text: Retrograde jovian irregulars: '160 +- 60 retrograde jovian moons with m_r < 24' and '600 retrograde jovian irregulars (within a factor of 2) down to 25.7th magnitude' (Sec. 3.5); differential luminosity function of the debiased detections from m_r = 23.75 to 25.75 with alpha = 0.29 +- 0.15 (Sec. 3.4, abstract); characterisation limit (50% detection efficiency) m_r = 25.7 (Sec. 3.1). The model here: 440 = 600 - 160 moons between m_r 24.0 and 25.7, distributed as dN/dm ~ 10^(0.29 m). Prograde jovian irregulars are not in this model (the paper debiases the retrograde population only).

completenessStatement.text: 'Jupiter's outer satellites are complete to about 2 km' (Sec. 1, citing Sheppard et al. 2023; albedo 0.1). Not used as a number: the limit is found by comparing the catalogue with the model.

model.orbitDistribution: ASSUMPTION: no bias-corrected orbit distribution was found in the published sources reviewed by the synthetic-rules audit. f(a, e, i) is that of the known moons of the class brighter than the limit (MPC osculating elements), in cells of 0.01-0.02 au x 0.1 x 5 deg; a, e, i uniform inside a cell; node, argument of pericentre and mean anomaly uniform.

albedo.text: Measured visible albedos of real irregular moons of the same planet and class: the seven retrograde jovians NEOWISE measured (Ashton et al. 2020 use 0.04, 'the average retrograde jovian albedo from Grav et al. 2015'); for Saturn, Phoebe, Albiorix and Siarnaq (Ashton et al. 2025 take their median, 0.06). Kalyke and Praxidike, Albiorix and Siarnaq come from stacked W3 or W4 detections only.

model.colour: No machine-readable colours of irregular moons are transcribed (photometry stage, grav-2015 note); a synthetic irregular moon is grey (the solar colour), as the real irregular moons are drawn.
model.motion: fixed two-body Kepler elements about the planet-system barycentre (system GM, naif-gm-de440), translated with the host ephemeris; no solar perturbation, oblateness or other-moon forces.
model.positionUncertainty: Individual true position and omitted-force position budget for this object/viewpoint are unknown. Heliocentric comparison uses Sun and product perturbers' Newtonian forces (omits 1PN/J2/nongrav); moon comparison uses host gravity and differential solar gravity (omits J2/other moons). These historical samples do not certify another catalogue, epoch or window.
model.method: ashton-2020-jupiter: survey luminosity law conditioned on MPC known counts; orbit distribution uses bright known-member templates without a survey selection correction. ASSUMPTION: no bias-corrected orbit distribution was found in the published sources reviewed by the synthetic-rules audit. f(a, e, i) is that of the known moons of the class brighter than the limit (MPC osculating elements), in cells of 0.01-0.02 au x 0.1 x 5 deg; a, e, i uniform inside a cell; node, argument of pericentre and mean anomaly uniform.
model.uncertainty: Ashton et al. 2020 §3.5 normalization: 600 within a factor of 2 at the faint anchor, 160 +/- 60 at the bright anchor; slope +/- 0.15. The difference of anchors is not an independently measured unseen count. Known-member orbit templates are not debiased; individual existence is unknown.

objectsHeader.labels: Every known attribute of a synthetic object is `synthetic`; missing values are `unknown` (source: its population's model, the completeness proxy, the catalogue snapshot, and the measured but not selection-corrected attribute templates). Real objects are unchanged by this stage (their `estimated` values stay population statistics applied to a real object).
objectsHeader.seedRule: cell stream: PCG64 seeded with the first 16 bytes (little-endian integer) of sha256('<algorithm>|<seed>|<population modelId>|ia|ie|ii|ih'), split as [low 64 bits, high 64 bits, 0] (salt 1 for the attribute stream of model-realization populations); u0 = first 8 bytes of sha256(same string + '|round') / 2^64
objectsHeader.yieldRule: shown = the first floor(deficit + u0) candidates of the cell's stream that pass its current limits. Yield is aggregate, not one-to-one replacement of a discovery. With fixed model, limits and templates, increased eligible counts reduce group deficits (subject to cell rounding); catalogue refits can change limits, normalization, orbit and attribute templates and do not guarantee monotonic counts or stable identities.
objectsHeader.frame: heliocentric osculating elements, ecliptic and equinox J2000 (IAU 1976 obliquity to ICRF), at epochEt; populations with a `center` (irregular moons): osculating elements about that planet-system barycentre with mu = center.gm, same axes

grey.method: colorClass 255: no class; the object is drawn in the solar colour (grey), an assumption (irregular moons: no transcribed colours)

slopeParameterG.method: The conventional slope parameter of the H-G law (Bowell et al. 1989), the value the catalogue uses where no G is fitted; every synthetic object gets it.
